title: VCE Applied Computing: Software Development, Units 3 and 4

areas.title: Software development: programming
areas.assessment: School-assessed coursework: four teacher-designed programming modules, at least two with a GUI
areas.summary: Interpret requirements and designs, then write, validate, debug and test modules in a programming language.

areas.title: Software development: analysis and design
areas.summary: Analyse a need or opportunity, plan the project, document requirements in an SRS, and generate and evaluate designs.

areas.title: Software development: development and evaluation
areas.summary: Develop and test the designed solution, evaluate it, and assess how well the project plan worked.

areas.title: Cyber security: secure software development practices
areas.summary: Evaluate how an organisation develops software, identify security risks, and recommend controls and improvements.

groups.title: Terms used in this study
groups.summary: The study design's glossary. Every term is examinable.

groups.title: Problem-solving methodology
groups.summary: The four stages (analysis, design, development, evaluation), their activities, and what each stage documents.

kks.title: AI in programming
kks.summary: Emerging uses of AI in programming: prompting to generate code, AI-assisted debugging, testing and optimisation, and using these tools responsibly and ethically.
examples: Writing a prompt that states inputs, outputs and constraints
Checking AI-generated code before using it

kks.title: Interpreting solution requirements
kks.summary: Reading functional and non-functional requirements, constraints and scope to decide what a module must do.
examples: A requirement that totals are shown to two decimal places
A constraint that the program runs offline

kks.title: Design tools for modules
kks.summary: Tools that represent a module's design before it is coded.
kks.verify: Confirm the exact list of design tools named for U3O1.

kks.title: Data types
kks.summary: Choosing a data type for each item of data and justifying the choice.
examples: Currency as floating point to two decimal places
Numbers stored as text sort as 1, 101, 15, 3, 5
kks.verify: Confirm the list of data types (character, string, integer, floating point, Boolean).

kks.title: Data structures
kks.summary: One-dimensional arrays, two-dimensional arrays and records: how each is organised and when each suits.
examples: A 1D array of scores indexed by integer
A 2D array indexed by row and column
A record with named fields of mixed types
kks.verify: Confirm whether associative arrays or lists are also named.

kks.title: Data sources
kks.summary: Plain text, delimited (CSV) and XML files: their structure, when each suits, and why XML's self-describing tags make it extensible.
examples: A log written as plain text lines
A CSV export from a spreadsheet
An XML file whose tags name each field

kks.title: Object-oriented programming
kks.summary: Abstraction, encapsulation, generalisation and inheritance; classes and objects; access modifiers.
examples: A Vehicle superclass generalising Car and Truck
Private attributes reached through public methods
Public, private, protected and default access

kks.title: Features of a programming language
kks.summary: Variables and constants, scope, control structures, operators, functions, procedures, methods, classes, GUI elements and file operations.
kks.verify: Confirm the list of language features.

kks.title: Naming conventions
kks.summary: Hungarian notation, camel case and snake case for variables, interface controls and code structures.

kks.title: Validation
kks.summary: Existence, type and range checks on input data.

kks.title: Internal documentation
kks.summary: Comments that state a module's purpose, its key features and why processing choices were made.
examples: A header comment stating a function's purpose
A comment justifying a binary search over a linear one

kks.title: Sorting and searching
kks.summary: Selection sort, quick sort, linear search and binary search; their relative efficiency; choosing a search from the data's order and the requirements.
examples: Quick sort is usually faster than selection sort on large lists

kks.title: Types of errors
kks.summary: Syntax, logic and runtime errors, including overflow, index out of range, type mismatch and divide by zero, and how error handling and extra checks reduce them.
examples: Reading element 10 of a 10-element zero-based array

kks.title: Debugging and testing
kks.summary: Breakpoints, debugging output statements and commenting out code; test cases, test data and test tables with expected and actual output.
examples: Setting a breakpoint inside a loop
A test table with expected and actual output
kks.verify: Confirm whether trace tables are named; otherwise treat tracing as desk-checking toward test tables.

kks.title: Why software projects happen
kks.summary: The reasons individuals and organisations commission software: solving a problem, meeting a need, taking an opportunity.
examples: Meeting a new legal reporting duty

kks.title: The project brief
kks.summary: What a brief documents about the problem, need or opportunity.

kks.title: Gantt charts
kks.summary: Planning with Gantt charts: tasks, durations, sequencing, dependencies, milestones and the critical path.
examples: A task that can't start until testing ends
The longest chain of dependent tasks

kks.title: Data collection techniques
kks.summary: Collecting data about needs and requirements, and choosing a technique to suit each stakeholder group.

kks.title: Functional and non-functional requirements
kks.summary: What the solution must do versus the qualities it must have.

kks.title: Constraints
kks.summary: Conditions that limit the solution.
examples: Technical: must run on existing tablets
kks.verify: Confirm the list of constraint types.

kks.title: Scope
kks.summary: The boundaries of the solution: what it will and will not do.
examples: The app will take bookings but will not process payments

kks.title: Analytical tools
kks.summary: Context diagrams, data flow diagrams and use case diagrams, including their notation and common convention errors.

kks.title: Software requirements specification
kks.summary: The purpose and contents of an SRS.
kks.verify: Confirm the listed contents of an SRS.

kks.title: Legal requirements
kks.summary: Key legal requirements for intellectual property, ownership and the privacy of data.

kks.title: File management
kks.summary: Naming, versioning, backing up, archiving and securely disposing of project files.

kks.title: Generating design ideas
kks.summary: Ideation techniques and tools for generating design ideas.
kks.verify: Confirm the ideation techniques and tools named.

kks.title: Efficiency, effectiveness and evaluation criteria
kks.summary: What makes a solution efficient and effective, and criteria for evaluating design ideas and solutions.

kks.title: Detailed design tools
kks.summary: Data dictionaries, mock-ups, object descriptions, IPO charts and pseudocode for detailed designs.
examples: A data dictionary listing name, type, size and description
An IPO chart for one module

kks.title: User experience characteristics
kks.summary: Affordance, interoperability, security and usability as characteristics of a user experience.
examples: Exporting to a format another system reads

kks.title: Design principles
kks.summary: Principles that shape a solution's appearance and functionality.
kks.verify: Confirm the list of design principles.

kks.title: Efficient and effective solutions
kks.summary: Qualities of efficient and effective solutions, and user-centred design.
examples: Fewer steps to complete a task
Designing with users' needs at the centre

kks.title: Data for input, storage and output
kks.summary: Choosing data types, data structures and data sources for input, storage and output.
examples: Reading a CSV into an array of records

kks.title: Language features in development
kks.summary: Using the features of a programming language to build the solution.

kks.title: Established and innovative approaches
kks.summary: Code repositories, APIs and libraries (and the risk when one changes or access is revoked), and AI-based coding assistants.
examples: A mapping API that changes its terms
A shared repository with commit history

kks.title: Validation techniques
kks.summary: Applying validation to the developed solution.
examples: Existence, type and range checks on a booking form

kks.title: Debugging and alpha testing
kks.summary: Debugging techniques and alpha testing by the developers.
examples: Testing each module against a test table
Using breakpoints to find a logic error

kks.title: Beta testing
kks.summary: Choosing a user group, writing test plans and scenarios, observing, and documenting results.
examples: Recruiting users who match the target audience
A scenario that walks through a booking

kks.title: Evaluation strategies
kks.summary: Features of an evaluation strategy: which criteria, when evaluation happens, and who is responsible.
examples: A survey of users two weeks after launch
kks.verify: Confirm the listed features of an evaluation strategy.

kks.title: Applying evaluation criteria
kks.summary: Techniques for applying evaluation criteria, including collecting evaluation data.
examples: Timing how long a task takes

kks.title: Project plan disruptions
kks.summary: Factors that affect how well a project plan works: scope creep, personnel changes and technical issues.
examples: The client adds a feature mid-project

kks.title: Recording progress
kks.summary: Annotations and adjustments, logs and journals, and project management software.
examples: Annotating a Gantt chart with actual dates

kks.title: Assessing the project plan
kks.summary: Judging how effective a project plan was.

kks.title: Organisational goals and objectives
kks.summary: The goals and objectives of medium and large organisations, and how software supports them.
examples: An objective to cut processing time by 20%

kks.title: In-house versus external development
kks.summary: Advantages and disadvantages of developing software in-house or with an external developer.
examples: In-house keeps control of the code
External brings expertise but less control

kks.title: Vulnerabilities in development environments
kks.summary: Vulnerabilities and risks in insecure software development environments.
examples: Development, testing and production sharing one environment
An insider misconfiguration exposing code and data
kks.verify: Confirm the listed vulnerabilities and risks.

kks.title: Security controls
kks.summary: Physical and software controls that protect development practices and data.

kks.title: Threat modelling
kks.summary: Principles of threat modelling applied to software development.
kks.verify: Confirm the threat modelling steps and their names.

kks.title: Evaluating security of development practices
kks.summary: Criteria for evaluating how secure an organisation's development practices are.
examples: Is access granted by least privilege?

kks.title: Legislation and frameworks
kks.summary: Laws and frameworks that govern data and security in software development.
kks.verify: Confirm the exact set of Acts and frameworks.

kks.title: Ethical issues
kks.summary: Ethical issues in software development.

kks.title: Reducing threats and risks
kks.summary: Measures that reduce or remove threats and risks to development practices and data.

kks.title: Recommending improvements
kks.summary: Making recommendations to improve an organisation's software development practices.
examples: Introduce mandatory code review before merging
Move secrets out of source code
